title: Probing-and-Rollback Harness for Safe Cost-Profile Applies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight probing and rollback harness that can safely apply batching/caching cost profiles to live traffic while preserving latency/throughput SLOs. The harness will run incremental micro-probes, exercise SLO-aware routing and RTT-aware throttles, perform streaming anomaly detection on tail latency and throughput stability, and orchestrate automated rollback or gradual ramp when thresholds are violated. This ticket covers prototype runtime hooks, console integration for probing visualization, and an automated rollback playbook for operators.
background: We have multiple initiatives that recommend more aggressive batching and KV caching to reduce per-token cost. Prior rollouts have occasionally caused tail latency regressions under specific traffic patterns (short conversational bursts, multi-turn long-context requests). Existing rollout tooling handles canaries by traffic percentage, but lacks micro-probing to detect tail behavior and no automated RTT-aware throttles or rapid rollback orchestration tied to our anomaly detector. This harness ties recommendations to a safe apply workflow so OptimizeFlow suggestions can be applied with SLO guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime: implement a probe mode that can apply a candidate cost-profile to a small set of traffic shards (1-3%) and emit a probe stream with detailed per-token latency, queue time, and KV hit-rate metrics for at least 30 minutes.
Routing: implement SLO-aware routing rules that temporarily route high-risk traffic (short seq) away from aggressive profiles during probe windows using policy tags.
Throttles: build an RTT-aware soft-throttle that reduces batch size or disables batching for shards where p99 latency increases by >15% within a 5-minute window.
Anomaly Detection: integrate DEWMA-based streaming detector that triggers rollback when tail latency or throughput drop exceeds configured thresholds and confidence windows.
Rollback Orchestration: automated rollback action that reverts profile, drains KV cache as needed, and sends annotated incident event to Console with runbook link and PR reference.
Console: probe dashboard shows live probe traces, delta metrics compared to baseline, and a one-click abort/approve control for operators.
Docs & Runbook: simple runbook for on-call describing probe interpretation, manual rollback steps, and escalation contacts.
Tests: end-to-end integration test that simulates a latency regression pattern and verifies rollback triggers within 10 minutes.
Performance: normal control-plane overhead of probe flow must be <2% of baseline CPU/latency impact on serving nodes.
progress_updates: 2025-10-10: Design review completed. Chosen approach: 3-stage probe -> ramp -> stable. Decided to use DEWMA for streaming anomaly detection because it is resilient to bursty traffic and cheap to compute in the runtime agent.
2025-10-17: Prototype runtime hooks merged to feature branch 'probe-harness'. Added probe-mode flag on profile apply and basic per-request tagging to flow-probe telemetry.

2025-10-22: Implemented RTT-aware soft-throttle logic (initial): measures moving p50/p95/p99 per-shard RTT; if p99 delta > 10% for two consecutive 60s windows, throttle applied to reduce batch-by-factor 0.5.
2025-10-29: Console mockups complete and synced with PM (Jamal Lee). Added probe visualization panel placeholder and abort button wiring (backend endpoints created).

2025-11-02: Integration tests added for simulated regression pattern; initial false-positive rate acceptable but tuning required for low-traffic shards. Next: improve confidence window and add traffic-weighted thresholds.
implementation_notes: Probe windows are non-blocking: probe shards are chosen by hash of user ID and can be rotated each hour to spread impact.
We will prefer soft rollback first: if KV cache mismatch causes quality regressions, we should allow cache warming time (default 5m) before full rollback unless latency SLOs are breached.
Store probe state in ConfigStore with TTL so failed probes automatically expire and do not linger across restarts.
Leverage existing metrics pipeline: publish probe.delta_{p50,p95,p99}, probe.kv_hit_rate, probe.batch_size to metrics namespace 'optflow.probe'.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Low-traffic customers may cause noisy signals (high variance). Mitigation: use traffic-weighted anomaly thresholds and require minimum sample count before action.
Risk: Over-eager rollback could cause oscillation. Mitigation: implement cooldown window (default 10m) and exponential backoff on re-applies.
Risk: KV cache warms slowly causing economic rollback misses. Mitigation: provide a cache-warm policy to pre-populate likely prefixes for probe shards and measure kv-warm progress.
Risk: Console operators misinterpret probe deltas. Mitigation: annotated deltas with expected noise ranges and example failure signatures in the runbook.
open_questions: What is the default probe shard size for low-volume customers? (proposed: 1% but may increase to 3% for short-burst traffic).
Should the soft-throttle reduce batch size linearly or switch to a conservative precomputed 'safe profile'?
How do we annotate multi-tenant shards where one tenant spike could affect another's p99? Consider tenant-aware isolation or routing.
next_steps: Tune DEWMA parameters for p99 detection and add adaptive sample thresholding based on request rate.
Finish console abort/approve UI and hook authorization via RBAC so only operators can abort auto-rollbacks.
Add e2e test that simulates cross-tenant burst to validate tenant-aware routing decision logic.
Schedule runbook review with on-call and support (target: 2025-11-12).

Sofia Chen (SRE) 2025-10-18: Can we expose an emergency 'panic button' that force-drains aggressive profiles globally? We'll need gracefulness for active KV sessions.
Design review (Lina Park) 2025-10-23: Console mockups look good; recommend adding a timeline slider to replay probe period and highlight anomalous requests.
Code review (Samir Gupta) 2025-10-30: Left inline comments on probe tag propagation and potential perf hotspot at the metrics flush. Suggested batching metric writes per-second.
